newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy referendums invalidated by low turnout.
newsitem.headline: Italy referendums invalidated by low turnout.

text.p: Seven national referendums held in Italy on Sunday on issues ranging from hunting to privatisation failed to secure the turnout required to be valid, RAI state television said, quoting computer projections.

RAI said the initial computer projections estimated that only 30 to 32 percent of voters had cast ballots. More than 50 percent of Italy's 49 million eligible voters had to participate for the process to be valid.
Voter fatigue after three general elections in five years, media indifference and sweltering heat that sent Italians flocking to the beaches all appeared to have contributed to the low turnout.

Many politicians, while not openly opposing the exercise, had criticised the nature and number of referendums, arguing that the issues were trivial, beyond the understanding of most voters or so technical as to be best left to legislators.
Six of Sunday's referendums were championed by the minority Radical Party, which accused mainstream parties in the run-up to voting of conspiring to ensure a flop.

Voters were asked in the referendums whether they wanted to set two new restrictions on the careers of magistrates, limit rights to hunting, scrap the Italian journalists' guild, make conscientious objection easier, and remove the right of the Treasury to retain a controlling "golden share" in strategic privatised industries. The seventh referendum, proposed by some of Italy's regions, sought to abolish the Agriculture Ministry.
